# captured 2026-09-22
# exe: /home/ubuntu/.local/bin/auth0
# args: 
Build, manage and test your Auth0 integrations from the command line.

## For Agents and Automation

The Auth0 CLI now includes features for AI agents and automation:

  • Schema Discovery: Use the '--schema' flag on a create/update command to print
    its request payload schema. Add '--json' for machine-readable output.
    Example: auth0 actions create --schema --json

  • JSON Input: Use '--data' flag for programmatic resource creation/updates
    Example: auth0 actions create --data @action.json

  • Schema Validation: JSON inputs are validated locally before API calls
    Example: auth0 actions create --data '{"name":"my-action",...}'

See 'auth0 <resource> --help' for details on specific resources.
For agent integration guide, visit: https://github.com/auth0/auth0-cli

## Agent Mode

Agent mode makes every command's output machine-readable. The CLI enables it
automatically when it detects an AI agent. Force it with '--agent-mode' (or
AUTH0_AGENT_MODE=true) and turn it off with '--agent-mode=false' (or
AUTH0_AGENT_MODE=false).

In agent mode the CLI:

  • Prints results to stdout as JSON, and streams (for example 'auth0 logs tail')
    as newline-delimited JSON, one object per line.
  • Keeps stderr clean: human hints and progress messages are suppressed, so on
    success stderr is empty and on failure it carries only a JSON error envelope
    ({"error":{"code","reason","message","status","details"}}). Because that envelope
    is the only thing on stderr, even a merged stdout+stderr stream stays parseable.
  • Disables interactive prompts and colors.
  • Prefers machine (client-credentials) login, which needs no browser:
    'auth0 login --domain <domain> --client-id <id> --client-secret <secret>'.
    A bare 'auth0 login' still works but requires a human: the CLI emits the device
    verification URL and code as a JSON object on stdout, then waits while a person
    approves it in a browser.
  • Exits 0 on success and 130 when interrupted; every other failure exits 1, so
    scripts that treat any non-zero exit as failure keep working. The specific
    failure class (usage, auth, validation, not_found, conflict, rate_limit, api) is carried
    by the JSON error envelope's "code" field, not by the exit code.


Before using the CLI, you'll need to login:

  $ auth0 login

Usage:
  auth0 <resource> <operation> [parameters...] [flags]

Available Resources:
  login           Authenticate the Auth0 CLI 
  logout          Log out of a tenant's session 
  tenants         Manage configured tenants 
  apps            Manage resources for applications [clients]
  acul            Advanced Customization the Universal Login experience 
  users           Manage resources for users 
  rules           Manage resources for rules 
  actions         Manage resources for actions 
  apis            Manage resources for APIs [resource-servers]
  client-grants   Manage client grants [grants]
  roles           Manage resources for roles 
  orgs            Manage resources for organizations [organizations]
  universal-login Manage the Universal Login experience [ul]
  phone           Manage phone providers 
  email           Manage email settings and configure email providers 
  domains         Manage custom domains 
  quickstarts     Quickstart support for getting bootstrapped [qs]
  protection      Manage resources for attack protection [attack-protection, ap]
  test            Try your Universal Login box or get a token 
  logs            View tenant logs 
  api             Makes an authenticated HTTP request to the Auth0 Management API 
  terraform       Manage terraform configuration for your Auth0 Tenant [tf]
  event-streams   Manage Event Stream 
  forms           Manage Forms 
  flows           Manage Flows 
  network-acl     Manage network ACL settings 
  connections     Manage resources for connections 
  tenant-settings Manage tenant settings 
  token-exchange  Manage token exchange profiles [te]
  sessions        Manage resources for sessions 
  refresh-tokens  Manage resources for refresh tokens 
  guardian        Manage multi-factor authentication (Guardian) 
  commands        Discover every CLI command in one place, for humans and AI agents 
  agent           Manage Auth0 AI capabilities 
  completion      Setup autocomplete features for this CLI on your terminal 

Flags:
      --agent-mode      Output JSON, disable prompts and colors.
                        Auto-enabled for AI agents; set
                        AUTH0_AGENT_MODE=false to disable.
      --debug           Enable debug mode.
  -h, --help            Help for auth0.
      --no-color        Disable colors.
      --no-input        Disable interactivity.
      --tenant string   Specific tenant to use.
  -v, --version         Version for auth0.

Use "auth0 [command] --help" for more information about a command.
Use "auth0 commands" for an overview of every command, and add --json to any --help for machine-readable output.
